paper_metadata.title: Solving General QUBOs with Warm-Start QAOA via a Reduction to Max-Cut

summary: The paper benchmarks warm-start QAOA on 16-variable QUBOs mapped to 17-qubit Max-Cut instances, using GW2/GW3 and BM2/BM3 warm-starts against QUBO-relaxed baselines over 1000 synthetic instances per problem family. At depth p=5, GW2 reaches approximation ratios up to 0.9993 and ground-state probability up to 0.9215 on portfolio optimization, but the paper reports no quantum speedup and all results are from a custom simulator rather than hardware.

experiments.description: Warm-start QAOA benchmark on QUBO instances mapped to Max-Cut, comparing GW2/GW3 and BM2/BM3 warm-starts against QUBO-relaxed warm-starts across random QUBOs, TSP, portfolio optimization, and MIS instances at depths p=0..5.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: QAOA parameters optimized; for each circuit the optimization loop was run 10 times and the best-cost parameter set was selected

hyperparameters.QAOA_restart_initialization: for p=1, 10 uniform random initializations; for p>1, 9 uniform random initializations plus 1 best-performing initialization from depth p-1

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Warm-start initial states derived from SDP/QUBO relaxations; QAOA angles initialized with 10 restarts (uniform random for p=1, mostly random plus best previous-depth seed for p>1)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary variables encoded as qubits; QUBOs are mapped to an equivalent Max-Cut/Ising instance by introducing one auxiliary variable/qubit, so an n-variable QUBO becomes an (n+1)-qubit Max-Cut problem
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize x^T Q x for QUBO; equivalent Max-Cut/Ising objective after reduction
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty terms used for constrained problems (TSP, portfolio optimization, MIS); QUBO-to-Max-Cut reduction introduces an auxiliary variable; warm-starts use SDP/QUBO relaxations
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_Q^Q = sum_{i,j} Q_ij ((1-Z_i)/2)((1-Z_j)/2); Max-Cut Hamiltonian H_A^M = -(1/4) sum_{i,j} A_ij Z_i Z_j

problem_instance.description: Four benchmark families: random QUBOs, 5-city TSP, portfolio optimization, and MIS on Erdős–Rényi and Newman–Watts–Strogatz graphs
problem_instance.dataset_name: Random QUBOs, TSP, Portfolio Optimization, MIS-GNP, MIS-NWS

dataset_specification.random_qubos: 16-variable symmetric Q matrices with upper-triangular entries sampled from Uniform[-1,1] or discrete {−1,1]
dataset_specification.tsp: 5 points sampled uniformly from [-1,1]^2; fully connected symmetric TSP
dataset_specification.portfolio_optimization: 16 assets, geometric Brownian motion over 250 time steps, budget B=8, q=0.5

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: TSP uses rotational symmetry breaking by fixing x_0=1; portfolio uses simulated prices to compute covariance matrix and mean returns; MIS graphs are rejection-sampled until connected
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 1000 instances generated per problem type; depth-0 evaluated on all 1000 instances; 10 of those 1000 selected for depths p=1..5; metrics averaged and reported with standard deviations

implementation_details.classical_solver: L-BFGS-B for QUBO-relaxed warmstart; COBYLA for QAOA parameter optimization
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: SDP/QUBO relaxations, random basis sampling for GWk, local optimization for non-convex QUBO-relaxed warmstart
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Map Max-Cut solution back to original QUBO variables; select best of 10 QAOA restarts by cost

speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum speedup claim is made; the paper reports empirical warm-start performance comparisons on a custom simulator.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: QAOA depth-p circuit with p layers; asymptotic convergence discussed as p→∞ for warm-started QAOA
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: QUBO-relaxed warmstart is NP-hard in general; convex only for negative semidefinite Q

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: At least 17 logical qubits for the benchmarked instances, depth up to p=5, plus a classical outer-loop optimizer and warm-start preprocessing.
limiting_factors: No QPU data; only custom simulation
No demonstrated quantum speedup over classical baselines
Performance is problem-dependent and often comparable to or worse than QUBO-relaxed baselines
Warm-start preprocessing is classical and substantial
Problem sizes are small (16-variable QUBOs, 5-city TSP, 16-asset portfolio, 16-node MIS)

notes: num_qubits inferred as 17 because the paper states each benchmark QUBO has 16 variables and the QUBO-to-Max-Cut mapping introduces one auxiliary qubit/variable.
hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper reports a custom QAOA simulator and no real QPU.
circuit_depth reported as p=0..5; maximum depth recorded as 5.
The paper reports empirical comparisons of warm-start QAOA against QUBO-relaxed classical warm-starts, but does not claim a practical quantum advantage.
Results are mixed: GW2 is better on some approximation-ratio cases, while QUBO-relaxed is better or comparable on others; all experiments are on a custom simulator.
